Yoki asosiy fayllar joylashgan papkani tanlang — quyidagi “Asosiy Generals papkasi” tugmasidan foydalaning.
Crash va engine loglari ilovaning yopiq xotirasida saqlanadi va yuqoridagi “Loglarni ko‘rish” orqali ochiladi. Android ularni oddiy fayl menejerlaridan yashiradi.

Ushbu sozlamalar ilovasi, log ko‘ruvchi va papka tanlagich tilini o‘zgartiradi. O‘yinning o‘z tili alohida sozlama — o‘yin papkasida mavjud tilni tanlang yoki til paketini yuklang. “Tizim tili” telefon tilidan foydalanadi.
O‘yin matni: bu sozlamaga bog‘liq emas (o‘yinning registry.ini tili yoki standart ingliz tili ishlatiladi).
O‘yin matni: ham o‘zgartirildi (o‘yin papkasida data/%1$s/generals.csf topildi).
O‘yin matni: o‘zgartirilmadi — o‘yin papkasida data/%1$s/generals.csf topilmadi, shuning uchun o‘yin o‘z tilini saqlaydi.
Ekran o‘lchamiga mos ravishda menyu tugmalari va yozuvlari matnini kattalashtiradi yoki kichraytiradi.
30 Hz matches every earlier build of this port. Android-to-Android matches work on it, but a match against a Windows player will desynchronise.
60 Hz matches the Windows GeneralsOnline client, which is what makes cross-play possible. It doubles the simulation work per second, so a slower device may run the game below full speed.

The tick rate is fixed when the engine is built, so the app carries both versions and loads the one you pick here. The change takes effect the next time you start the game. Both players in a match must be on the same rate.
Simulyatsiya tezligi saqlandi. Keyingi ishga tushirishda qo‘llanadi.

The Windows client simulates at 60 Hz, and a 30 Hz client cannot stay in step with it, so cross-play has switched this device to 60 Hz. It takes effect the next time you start the game.\n\nThis doubles the simulation work per second. If the game runs slowly, turn cross-play off or set the rate back to 30 Hz under Graphics — but then you can only play against other Android players on 30 Hz.
Simulation rate: 30 Hz — cannot hold sync with a PC
Simulation rate: 60 Hz — matches the PC client

Which graphics API the game uses. Takes effect the next time you launch the game, not live.

OpenGL ES (default): a native renderer written for this port. It is the default because it works on every device tested so far, including ones where Vulkan renders corrupted graphics. Start here; only change it if you have a reason to.

OpenGL ES + ANGLE: the same renderer, but routed through Google's ANGLE, which translates it to Vulkan, instead of your phone's own GLES driver. ANGLE is bundled inside this app, so it needs no minimum Android version and no system setting. Often faster once running, though a menu with many controls (Skirmish options) can stutter the first time it opens while ANGLE compiles what it needs; it does not stutter again until you leave and reopen that menu.

Vulkan: the original backend, through DXVK's Direct3D 8 to Vulkan translation. Faster than the others on phones whose driver handles it well, typically recent Snapdragon. But it depends entirely on that driver, and on some GPUs it produces magenta patches, distorted geometry or corrupted menus that no setting here can fix — PowerVR BXM and Samsung Xclipse have both been reported. If Vulkan looks wrong on your device, that is what the default is for.

The Custom Vulkan Driver and DXVK Config sections only appear when Vulkan is selected.

Loads a Vulkan driver (a Mesa Turnip build) instead of your phone's built-in one, the same technique Winlator and AetherSX2 use. DXVK itself now only needs Vulkan 1.1, but some older Qualcomm Adreno stock drivers report even less (or have other bugs) — this Turnip build can let those phones run the game anyway. On a qualifying Adreno phone this is applied automatically — "Reset to Recommended" restores that automatic choice after you've imported something else.

This does NOT help Mali, PowerVR, or other non-Adreno GPUs — but those don't need it either: most Mali GPUs (Mali-G76, Mali-G57, and similar) already meet DXVK's Vulkan 1.1 requirement natively, no driver swap needed. This option is Adreno-only because Turnip only targets Adreno hardware, not because other GPUs are unsupported.

"Import Driver" lets you override the automatic choice with your own adrenotools-format driver .zip (for example from K11MCH1/AdrenoToolsDrivers or The412Banner/Banners-Turnip on GitHub). Takes effect next launch, not live.
Maxsus drayver faol emas — telefonning o‘z Vulkan drayveri ishlatilmoqda.
Reset done. The recommended driver for this device was reapplied.

Edits dxvk.conf directly, the same file the engine reads on startup — no rebuild needed, takes effect next launch. Useful settings if the game feels slow on your device:

d3d9.samplerAnisotropy = 2 (or 0 to disable) — lower than the default 16 to reduce GPU work on weaker hardware.
dxvk.hud = fps,drawcalls,submissions,pipelines — shows a small on-screen performance overlay.
dxvk.logLevel = none — keep this unless asked to change it; more verbose levels slow the game down.

One "key = value" per line. An invalid line is simply ignored by DXVK, so a typo won't break the game — worst case your change has no effect.
No bundled default dxvk.conf found in this build.

These turn on extra logging for bug reports — leave them all off for normal play, they can slow the game down or produce large logs. If someone reporting an issue asks you to turn one on, enable it, reproduce the problem, then use \"View Logs\" above to send the result.
Buning uchun avval o‘yin papkasini tanlang

Very detailed internal logging (UI, fonts, INI files) for chasing a specific hang or bug. Can grow to a huge log (50–100+ MB) over a long session — use \"Performance summary\" instead if you only need FPS numbers. (gx_trace.txt)

Draws the touch layer\'s own state over the game: current gesture, where your finger is, where the engine thinks the pointer is, and the camera scroll anchor. Turn this on to report control problems — a runaway map, a ghost building in the wrong place, an ability aiming somewhere you did not touch. (gx_touch_debug.txt)

Adds one short line per second showing where frame time goes (radar, audio, network, game logic, rendering). Safe to leave on for a whole play session — turn this on for FPS/slowdown reports. (gx_perf.txt)

Records what the sound system is doing: music and speech buffer levels, movie audio, and every source that starts or stops. Turn this on if you are asked for an audio log after reporting missing, stuttering or silent sound. (gx_audio_trace.txt)

Records every request the game makes to the GeneralsOnline servers, with the reply it got. Turn this on if sign-in, the lobby or matchmaking fails from inside the game. The launcher\'s own requests are always recorded; this adds the game\'s. It also turns on the cross-play desync diagnostics: the simulation checksums that are compared each interval, and, in a replay, the checksum of every single object. (gx_net_trace.txt)
Til paketi o‘rnatildi. Keyingi ishga tushirishda ishlatiladi.
%1$d ta til paketi o‘rnatildi: %2$s. Quyidagilardan birini tanlang.
Bu launcher tili uchun o‘yin matni paketi mavjud emas.
Bu til uchun hali paket yo‘q. Tarjimalar qabul qilinadi — loyiha ichidagi languages/README.md ni ko‘ring.
could not create the language folder in your game folder

O‘yin matni: Inglizcha — agar o‘yin papkasidagi .big fayl almashtirmasa
O‘yin papkasida hali til paketi topilmadi. Avval birini yuklang.
Shows FPS, draw calls, submissions, and pipeline count directly on screen and in the log. Turn this on for GPU performance reports. (dxvk_hud.txt)

Checks every graphics call for correctness — catches real rendering bugs but slows the game down noticeably. Only turn this on when asked to reproduce a specific crash or glitch, not for everyday play. (dxvk_validation.txt)

Adds extra startup details about how the game talks to your GPU driver (exact display format and settings negotiated). Turn this on when asked to track down a rendering glitch specific to your device. (dxvk_verbose_log.txt)
Tizimga kirilmagan — onlayn o‘yin uchun kerak.

1. "Select Game Folder" opens a folder browser on your phone's storage. Navigate to wherever you copied your own Command & Conquer Generals Zero Hour install (the folder containing INIZH.big, Data\, ZH_Generals\, etc.) and tap "Use This Folder".

2. If browsing looks empty, Android is asking for the "All files access" permission first — grant it in the screen that opens (this is a normal Android permission, no root involved).

3. "View Logs" shows the engine log and, if the game crashed, a native crash log — no computer or adb needed. Use the Share button there to send the log to yourself.

4. "Launch Game" starts the game with the folder you picked.

Tap Sign In. The first tap may ask to exempt this app from battery optimization -- allow it, then come back and tap Sign In again. A browser then opens to playgenerals.online, already carrying a one-time code for this device. Pick Steam, Discord, or GameReplays there, then just come back to this app; it finishes on its own.

Playing online needs two things the retail game does not ship: the community data patch, which decides whether a PC-hosted game will accept this device, and the community maps those games are played on. This fetches both from GeneralsOnline directly — no PC involved.
Off leaves the download in place but makes the game read retail data again, so PC-hosted games will refuse this device. Takes effect the next time the game starts.
Required for online play — tap Update
Games hosted from a PC will refuse this device until the community data patch is installed, and they are played on the community maps. Download both now? About 30 MB.
Removes only the files this download installed. Your own maps and saves are left alone.
Nothing to delete: there is no record of an install by this launcher.
Could not change the setting. Check that the game data folder is writable.
Games hosted by the Windows client normally refuse this device, because the two are different programs and their EXE checksums can never match.
Community data patch missing — tap Update

Reports the Windows client\'s EXE checksum so its games will accept you. That checksum is not anti-cheat — it is what keeps two machines that would compute the match differently from playing it together, so this can desync the game for everyone in the lobby. Turn it on for a PC you own, and only after copying that PC\'s INI data into this game folder so the two really do match.
Allow GeneralsZH to run in the background on the next screen, then come back and tap Sign In again -- otherwise Android may kill the sign-in check while you\'re in the browser.

Run through: the replay is simulated as fast as the phone allows, stops a little after the first mismatch or at the end, and returns here with the result. Watch from frame: fast-forwards to the frame, then plays normally.

Also writes the logic checksum of every frame to the log. Used to build a copy of a replay that the PC client checks frame by frame. Slower.

Mobile clients have no anti-cheat. To play together, the PC player has to turn anti-cheat off (GeneralsOnline AntiCheat or Easy Anti-Cheat) in the GeneralsOnline launcher: lobbies with a different anti-cheat cannot be joined from a phone, and a phone lobby cannot be joined from them.
Write game, crash and network logs to the device. Turn off to keep nothing in the background; the logs stay off until you turn this back on. Needed for bug reports.
